html:
Visoki Dečani is a Serbian Orthodox monastery in western Kosovo, built between 1327 and 1335 by King Stefan Dečanski and his son Stefan Dušan.

Its church, the largest medieval church in the Balkans, mixes Romanesque stonework in pale and red marble with Byzantine plans. Inside are more than a thousand painted scenes, one of the largest sets of frescoes from the Byzantine world. Dečani was among the richest foundations of the Nemanjić kings. NATO peacekeepers have guarded it since the Kosovo War, and it is on the UNESCO list of heritage in danger. It shows why Kosovo is sacred ground to Serbs.
sum: Visoki Dečani is a Serbian Orthodox monastery in western Kosovo, built between 1327 and 1335 by King Stefan Dečanski and his son Stefan Dušan.
